Rashi on Gittin 43b:10:2.english: He is emancipated - since it is like a sale, and the Rabbis penalized him:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:10:3.hebrew: נשקי - חותם וסי' עבדות שתולין לעבדים בצואריהם:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:10:3.english: Nashkei - A seal and a sign of servitude that they hang around the necks of slaves:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:11:1.hebrew: האריסין - ישראל שנעשה אריס לעובד כוכבים בקרקע העובד כוכבים, וקסבר: יש קנין לעובד כוכבים בארץ להפקיע מיד מעשר:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:11:1.english: The sharecroppers - A Jew who became a sharecropper for an idolater on the idolater's land, and [the Tanna] holds that an idolater has [valid] ownership in the Land [of Israel] to exempt [the produce] from tithes.

Rashi on Gittin 43b:11:2.english: A sharecropper - [One who works a field] for a half, a third, or a fourth [of the produce]:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:11:3.english: Tenant farmers - [one] who leased it [the field] from the idolater for such-and-such [an amount of] wheat per year:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:11:4.hebrew: ואריסי בתי אבות - כלומר, אריסות קבועה ועומדת מאבות, שהיו אבותיו של ישראל אריסין בקרקע זה לאבותיו של עובד כוכבים זה — אפ"ה לא הוי כקנוי לישראל, אלא של עובד כוכבים הוא, ופטור מן המעשר ישראל זה בחלקו:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:11:4.english: And family sharecroppers - That is to say, a permanent and enduring sharecropping [arrangement] from [their] ancestors, where the ancestors of a Jew were sharecroppers on this land for the ancestors of this idolater — even so, it is not [considered] as acquired by the Jew, rather it belongs to the idolater, and this Jew is exempt from the tithe on his portion:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:11:5.english: Even though he made for him - [meaning] for the Jew, his law:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:12:1.hebrew: זמן - אם לא פרעתיך לזמן פלוני, יהא חלוט לך:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:12:1.english: Time - [Meaning, he stipulated:] "If I do not pay you by such-and-such a time, it shall be permanently yours."

Rashi on Gittin 43b:13:1.hebrew: קשיא זמן אזמן - דגבי עבד חשיב לה מכירה, וגבי שדה לאו מכירה היא:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:13:1.english: [There is a] difficulty [between] time [and] time - For regarding a slave it is considered a sale, and regarding a field it is not a sale:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:13:2.english: This [is] when his time has arrived - this [refers to the case] regarding a slave:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:14:1.english: But with regard to a slave whose time has arrived - This is [phrased] as a question:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:14:2.hebrew: הא לגופא - גבי עבד, דקבע בו זמן לגופו, שאם לא יתן לו עד אותו זמן יהא גופו חלוט לעובד כוכבים, ומעכשיו היה משתעבד בו; וכיון דזלזל בתקנתא דרבנן, דאסרו למכור עבד לעובד כוכבים, קנסוהו, ואע"ג דלא מטא זימניה; וגבי שדה, דקבע לו זמן לפירות — שאמר לו: "עכשיו לא תאכל הפירות, ואם לא אפרע לך ליום פלוני, אכול פירות עד שאפרע מעותיך" — הלכך אפי' מטא זימניה לאו מכירה היא, וכ"ש בדלא מטא זימניה:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:14:2.english: This [refers] to [the slave] himself - Regarding a slave, where he set a time for his body — [stipulating] that if he does not pay him by that time, his body will be permanently transferred to the idolater, and from now on he was [already] subjugated to him; and since he treated lightly the enactment of the Rabbis, who forbade selling a slave to an idolater, they penalized him, even though his time has not arrived. And regarding a field, where he set a time for the produce — [saying to him:] "Now you shall not eat the produce, and if I do not pay you by such-and-such a day, eat the produce until I repay your money" — therefore, even when its time has arrived, it is not a sale, and all the more so when its time has not arrived:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:1:1.hebrew: ואין אני קורא בה אשת שני מתים - לומר: חציה היתה לזה וחציה לזה, ומכח שניהם היא באה; ואמרי' ביבמות (דף לא:): ג' אחין נשואין ג' נשים נכריות, ומת אחד מהם, ועשה בה השני מאמר ומת, חולצת ולא מתיבמת, שנאמר: "ומת אחד מהם" וגו' (דברים כ״ה:ה׳) — מי שעליה זיקת יבם א', ולא שעליה זיקת שני יבמין; וזו ע"י מאמר לא יצתה מזיקת יבום הראשון כולה, ובמקצתה חל עליה זיקת יבום השני; אבל הכא לא זיקת שנים עלה, דחד מנייהו קדושין גמורים, ודאידך לאו כלום; ומיהו משום פלוגתא דאמוראי דלעיל מספקא לן הי מנייהו הוו קדושין, והשתא דמתו להו, מתיבמת ללוי ממה נפשך כו':
Rashi on Gittin 43b:1:1.english: And I do not declare her to be the wife of two dead [men] - to say [that] half of her belonged to this one and half of her belonged to that one, and she comes [into levirate marriage] by virtue of both of them. And we say in Yevamot (31b): [If] three brothers were married to three unrelated women, and one of them died, and the second [brother] performed ma'amar [rabbinic betrothal of a yevamah] with her and died, she performs chalitzah and does not enter into levirate marriage, as it is stated: "And one of them dies" etc. (Deuteronomy 25:5) — [this applies to] one upon whom rests the levirate bond of one yavam, and not [one] upon whom rests the levirate bond of two yevamim; and this woman, through ma'amar, did not leave the levirate bond of the first completely, and in part the levirate bond of the second took effect upon her. But here, the [levirate] bond of two [brothers] is not upon her, for [the betrothal of] one of them is a complete betrothal, and [that] of the other is nothing; however, because of the dispute of the Amoraim above, we are in doubt which of them was [a valid] betrothal, and now that they have died, she enters into levirate marriage with Levi whichever way you look at it, etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:2:1.english: And she went back and was betrothed to Shimon - and it did not mention [Shimon] because [he is Reuven's] brother:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:2:2.hebrew: פקעו קדושי ראשון - אפי' למ"ד מקודשת, בא השחרור והפקיעה, ומקודשת לשני, שהרי נשתנה גופה והויא לה כקטן שנולד:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:2:2.english: The first betrothal was abrogated - Even according to the one who says she is betrothed [to the first man], the emancipation came and abrogated it, and she is betrothed to the second [man], for her body has changed and she is like a newborn child:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:2:3.hebrew: גמרו קדושי ראשון - ע"י השחרור גמרו, דעד עכשיו הבא עליה באשם ומלקות היה, אפילו מזיד; ומכאן ואילך הבא עליה במיתה:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:2:3.english: The first betrothal was completed - Through the emancipation it was completed, for until now, one who had relations with her was [liable] to a guilt-offering and lashes, even [if he acted] intentionally; and from now on, one who has relations with her [is liable] to death:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:3:1.hebrew: לא יומתו כי לא וגו' - ומוקמינן לה בחציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין, וס"ל דה"ק: אינן חייבין מיתה משום א"א כי לא חופשה לאחר קידושין, הא חופשה לבתר הכי — יומתו, דהוי לה אשת איש גמורה:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:3:1.english: They shall not be put to death, because [she was] not, etc. - And we establish it [as referring] to one who is half maidservant and half free woman, and he [Rabbi Zeira] holds that this is what [the verse] is saying: They are not liable for the death penalty on account of [adultery with] a married woman because she was not freed after betrothal; [however,] if she was freed afterward, they shall be put to death, for she has become a full-fledged married woman:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:4:1.hebrew: ה"נ - הא חופשה בתר אירוסין יומתו? וכי קידושין ראשונים כלום היו:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:4:1.english: So too - [if] she was freed after [her] betrothal, are they put to death? And were the first betrothals anything [of validity]?

Rashi on Gittin 43b:4:2.english: Rather, what have you to say - The implication of the verse means thus:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:4:3.english: But [if] she was freed and went back and was betrothed - they are put to death if she committed adultery with another [man]:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:5:1.hebrew: כר' יוחנן בן ברוקה - במס' יבמות:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:5:1.english: In accordance with [the opinion of] Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka - [This is stated] in Tractate Yevamot:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:5:2.english: Concerning both of them it states, etc. - [Meaning] that a woman is also commanded regarding [the mitzvah of] procreation:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:6:1.hebrew: מנהג הפקר היו נוהגין בה - בזנות, דלא היתה מיוחדת לאדם ולא היתה משמרת עצמה:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:6:1.english: They treated her in a licentious manner - with harlotry, for she was not designated for [any one] man and she did not guard herself:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:7:1.hebrew: יצא לחירות - אם ברח מן העובד כוכבים, או שקנסוהו ב"ד לפדותו — כדאמר לקמן דקונסים אותו לפדותו, וכשיפדנו לא ישתעבד לו — וקנס חכמים הוא, הואיל והפקיעו מן המצות. וכן לח"ל יצא לחירות, מפני שהוציאו מארץ לחוצה לארץ. ובגמרא מפרש את מי קנסו, אם את הלוקח או את המוכר:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:7:1.english: He goes out to freedom - if he fled from the idolater, or if the court penalized [the seller] to redeem him — as [the Gemara] says below, that they penalize him to redeem him, and when he redeems him he may not enslave him [again]. And it is a penalty [instituted by] the Sages, since he removed him from [the obligation of] the commandments. And likewise, [if one sells him] outside the Land [of Israel], he goes out to freedom, because he took him out from the Land [of Israel] to outside the Land. And in the Gemara, it explains whom they penalized: whether the buyer or the seller:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:8:1.english: Ino [his document] - [This means] a legal document:

Rashi on Gittin 43b:9:1.hebrew: לכשתברח - מן העובד כוכבים, אין לי עסק בך:
Rashi on Gittin 43b:9:1.english: When you escape - from the idolater, I have no business with you:

Tosafot on Gittin 43b:1:1.hebrew: ואין אני קורא בה אשת שני מתים - וא"ת: והכא מאי נפקא מינה אם היא אשת שני מתים? הא אמרינן בפ' ד' אחין (יבמות דף לא:) דזיקת שני יבמין דרבנן, גזירה שמא יאמרו שתי יבמות הבאות מבית אחד מתיבמות, וזה לא שייך הכא! וי"ל דהתם במאמר דרבנן הויא זיקת ב' יבמין דרבנן, אבל בעלמא הוי דאורייתא:
Tosafot on Gittin 43b:1:1.english: And I do not declare her to be the wife of two dead [men] - And if you ask: Here, what practical difference is there if she is the wife of two dead [men]? Do we not say in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Aḥin (Yevamot 31b) that [the prohibition against] the levirate bond of two levirs is rabbinic — a decree lest people say that two yevamot coming from one house may enter into levirate marriage — and this does not apply here! And one can answer that there, in the case of ma'amar, which is rabbinic, the levirate bond of two levirs is rabbinic; however, in general, it is biblical:

Tosafot on Gittin 43b:1:2.hebrew: מה נפשך אי קידושי ראובן כו' - פי' בקונטרס דמשום פלוגתא דאמוראי דלעיל, מספקא ליה הי מינייהו הוו קידושין. וקשה, דרב חסדא גופיה פשיטא ליה דהוו קידושין, ורבה בר רב הונא נמי חזר בו מכח דברי רב חסדא. ונראה, דמספקא ליה אי גמרי קדושי ראשון אי פקעי:
Tosafot on Gittin 43b:1:2.english: Whichever way [you look at it], if Reuven’s betrothal, etc. - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres that because of the dispute of the Amoraim above, [Rav Chisda] is in doubt as to which of them is a [valid] betrothal. And [this] is difficult, for to Rav Chisda himself it is obvious that it is a [valid] betrothal, and Rabbah bar Rav Huna also retracted on account of Rav Chisda’s words. And it appears that [Rav Chisda] is in doubt whether the betrothal of the first [brother] is completed or is uprooted:

Tosafot on Gittin 43b:2:1.hebrew: גמרו קידושי ראשון - והא דאמרי' בפ"ק דקידושין (דף ז.): "בהמה של שני שותפין, הקדיש חציה וחזר ולקחה והקדיש חציה כו'" — הא לא הקדישה, לא גמרי? שאני התם, דאפשר שתרעה ויהיו חציה דמיה הקדש וחציה חולין; אבל הכא, דאי אפשר שתהא חציה מקודשת, ד"כי יקח איש אשה" כתיב, לא חצי אשה — מסתבר למימר: או גמרי או פקעי. ואע"ג דהתם מדמי למקדש חצי אשה, לא קשה מידי, דמייתי שפיר דהיכא דאיכא דעת אחרת לא פשטי בכולה. אי נמי איכא למימר, דבהמה של שני שותפין ששייר בקניינו קצת — שהרי בהמה היתה בת הקדש — לפיכך לא גמרי; אבל הכא, חציה שפחה לא היתה בכלל קידושין:
Tosafot on Gittin 43b:2:1.english: The first betrothal was completed - And [regarding] that which we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (7a): "[If] an animal belonged to two partners, [and one] consecrated half of it, and then went and bought [the other half] and consecrated half of it, etc." — [this implies that if] he did not consecrate [the second half], [the first consecration] does not complete! It is different there, because it is possible for it to graze [until it develops a blemish], and half of its value will be consecrated and half of it non-sacred. But here, where it is impossible for half of her to be betrothed — for "When a man takes a wife" is written, [and] not half a wife — it is logical to say [that] either [the betrothal] completes or it is abrogated. And even though there [the Gemara] compares [it] to one who betroths half a woman, it is not difficult at all, for it brings [the comparison] properly [to show] that wherever there is another domain, [the consecration or betrothal] does not spread to the whole. Alternatively, one can say that [in the case of] an animal of two partners, he left something over in his acquisition, for the animal was fit for consecration; therefore [the consecration] does not complete. But here, her maidservant half was not in the category of betrothal [at all]:

Tosafot on Gittin 43b:8:1.hebrew: אבל אם כתב עליו אונו זהו שחרורו - וא"ת: הא דאמר אמימר לעיל (גיטין דף מ.), המפקיר עבדו אין לו תקנה, דאיסורא דאיכא גביה לא מצי מקני ליה, וכאן משמע דיש לו תקנה בשטר; ועל כרחך לא משחרר ליה עד שיברח, דאי לאלתר חייל השחרור, היכי מזבין ליה ומסר ליה לעובד כוכבים להשתעבד בו? וי"ל: דלא דמי למפקיר, דעובד כוכבים לא קני ליה אלא למעשה ידיו, ואכתי פש ליה גבי ישראל ממונא, דקני ליה לקנס ולוולדות, ולא הפקיעו ממנו חכמים עד אחר שיכתוב לו גט שחרור:
Tosafot on Gittin 43b:8:1.english: But if he wrote a document for him, this is his emancipation - And if you ask: [Regarding] that which Amemar said above (Gittin 40a), [that] one who declares his slave ownerless has no remedy, because the ritual prohibition that remains with him cannot be conveyed to him, yet here it implies that he does have a remedy with a document; and perforce he does not emancipate him until he flees, for if the emancipation took effect immediately, how could he sell him and hand him over to the idolater to be enslaved by him? And one can answer: It is not comparable to one who declares [his slave] ownerless, for the idolater acquires him only for his labor, and monetary [rights] still remain with the Jew, for he owns him with respect to the fine and the offspring, and the Sages did not expropriate [this] from him until after he writes him a bill of manumission:
